subject: math

objective.text: Find unknown numbers on a number line. Use the distance between numbers and points you know.

explanations.title: Endpoints and zooming in
explanations.text: A number line has a left endpoint and a right endpoint. The left endpoint is often 0. You can zoom in on one piece, like 30 to 50. The other numbers are still there, just not written.

explanations.title: Hash marks and units
explanations.text: Hash marks are the small lines. A unit is the space between two hash marks. Count the spaces to count units. 5 hash marks make 4 units.

explanations.title: Find points with the unit value
explanations.text: Every unit on a number line has the same length. If you know one unit, you know them all. Count by that unit from a point you know to find the missing point.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Problem 1 and 2; Student Debrief

explanations.title: Cut a length in half
explanations.text: A hash mark in the middle is the same distance from both ends. Between 30 and 50 the middle is 40. Cut each half again to make 4 equal units of 5.

explanations.title: Difference between endpoints
explanations.text: Add the unit lengths to find the total distance. You can also subtract the small endpoint from the big endpoint. Both ways give the same difference.

examples.title: Number line from 30 to 50
examples.text: The endpoints are 30 and 50. There are 4 units. Each unit is 5. Count by fives: 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. Point A is 35 and Point B is 45. The difference is 20.

examples.title: Count up from 100
examples.text: A number line starts at 100. It has 4 units of 10. Count by tens: 100, 110, 120, 130, 140. Point E is 140. The difference is 40.

examples.title: Count back from 95
examples.text: A number line ends at 95. It has 4 units of 10. Count back by tens from 95. Point A is 55. The difference is 40.
